reason: The cited evidence does not address W-based HEAs, Ti-rich clusters, or their effect on thermal conductivity. E1 shows Hf effects on grain-boundary segregation and strength in an AlCrFeNiMo system, but not in a W-based HEA or at 800–1200 °C. E2 discusses lattice thermal conductivity of MoWTaTiZr but provides no data on Ti clustering or Hf addition. The key premises thus lack specific prior support from the cited passages.
premises: Ti-rich clusters in W-based HEAs act as effective phonon scattering centers, reducing lattice thermal conductivity.
Reducing Ti content by 10–15% will significantly reduce Ti-rich cluster formation.
Adding 0.5–1 at% Hf enhances grain-boundary cohesion and maintains high-temperature strength.
The proposed composition remains within a single-phase or benign two-phase regime as predicted by CALPHAD.
The modified composition will yield a 15–20% increase in lattice thermal conductivity at 800–1200 °C.
